key_insight: DECO is a sparse Mixture-of-Experts design that matches the accuracy of a dense Transformer with the same total parameter budget while drastically reducing on-device storage and memory-access costs, enabling high-performance inference on end-side devices.
problem_solved: Standard MoE increases total parameter count and memory traffic, creating storage and memory-access bottlenecks that prevent efficient deployment on resource-constrained end-side devices without sacrificing accuracy or latency.
method: Design a sparse MoE architecture that preserves total parameter capacity but only activates a small subset of expert parameters per token, keeping compute low while maintaining dense-comparable quality.
Reorganize expert parameters and memory layout for on-device friendliness (compact storage, fewer random accesses) so the large global parameter footprint no longer causes runtime/memory penalties.
Adopt lightweight routing and inference optimizations to minimize extra control overhead and latency during expert selection, enabling efficient end-side execution.
impact: DECO lets practitioners get the capacity benefits of MoE for higher model quality while meeting stringent on-device constraints (storage, memory bandwidth, compute, latency), making advanced models practical for edge and mobile deployment.
visual_elements: Side-by-side schematic: dense Transformer vs DECO MoE showing equal total parameters but fewer active weights and lower memory access for DECO

Scatter plot: accuracy (y) vs on-device cost metrics (x: storage or memory bandwidth) highlighting DECO's dense-comparable accuracy at reduced cost
paper_title: DECO: Sparse Mixture-of-Experts with Dense-Comparable Performance on End-Side Devices
paper_authors: Chenyang Song, Weilin Zhao, Xu Han, Chaojun Xiao, Yingfa Chen
